UK development finance lending trends reflect a stabilizing macroeconomic environment with a base rate around 3.5%, featuring monthly interest rates of 0.65% to 1.10%. Lenders are emphasizing integrated end-to-end funding facilities, stricter risk analysis, and growing support for SME brownfield and sustainable green-build projects.[](https://www.paragonbank.co.uk/blog/what-trends-are-we-likely-to-see-in-the-development-finance-industry-in-2025-) [[1]](https://www.paragonbank.co.uk/blog/what-trends-are-we-likely-to-see-in-the-development-finance-industry-in-2025-)[[2]](https://www.lendinvest.com/blog/the-2026-uk-property-development-market-viability-policy-and-the-sme-revival/)[[3]](https://abcfinance.co.uk/development-finance/)[[4]](https://diamondpropertyfinance.com/blogs/uk-property-development-finance-everything-you-need-to-know-in-2025/)[[5]](https://alternativebridging.co.uk/build-more-than-property-build-momentum-with-property-development-finance-uk/)Current Rates and LTV Parameters

- **Interest Rates** : Ground-up residential schemes typically range between 0.65% and 1.10% per month (approx. 8% to 13% annualized), varying by borrower experience and project complexity.[](https://www.fdcommercial.co.uk/finance-guide/development-finance-rates/) [[1]](https://www.fdcommercial.co.uk/finance-guide/development-finance-rates/)
- **Loan-to-GDV (LTGDV)** : Capped standardly at 65% to 70% of the completed gross development value, stretching slightly higher for seasoned developers.[](https://abcfinance.co.uk/development-finance/) [[1]](https://nmfinance.co.uk/your-complete-property-development-finance-guide-in-the-uk/)
- **Loan-to-Cost (LTC)** : Generally limited to 85% of total project costs, though experienced teams can access up to 90%.[](https://abcfinance.co.uk/development-finance/) 

Structural and Product Shifts

- **Integrated Facilities** : Lenders are shifting away from fragmented stage-by-stage borrowing, favoring single-facility structures that seamlessly blend construction finance with development exit products to minimize refinancing friction.[](https://alternativebridging.co.uk/build-more-than-property-build-momentum-with-property-development-finance-uk/) 
- **SME De-Risking** : Specialized institutions like [Shawbrook Bank](https://www.shawbrook.co.uk/property-finance/development-finance/) and other active regional funds are deploying targeted products alongside government-backed buyer initiatives (such as permanent high-LTV mortgage supports) to provide exit certainty.[](https://www.commercialtrust.co.uk/news/best-development-finance-lenders-2026/) [[1]](https://www.commercialtrust.co.uk/news/best-development-finance-lenders-2026/)
- **Green Financing** : Lenders continue expanding dedicated green lending lines, incentivizing energy-efficient standards and brownfield regeneration to align with upcoming environmental regulations.[](https://www.paragonbank.co.uk/blog/what-trends-are-we-likely-to-see-in-the-development-finance-industry-in-2025-) [[1]](https://www.evlo.co.uk/news/business/sustainable-finance-green-lending-initiatives/)[[2]](https://www.arcapita.com/media/x2jhbyyj/uk-real-estate-unlocking-opportunities.pdf)[[3]](https://digby-associates.co.uk/news/uk-green-mortgages-a-guide-and-latest-developments-2025/)[[4]](https://www.estatesgazette.co.uk/news/urban-partners-launches-e650m-regeneration-fund-targeting-uk-and-european-cities/)

If you would like to explore this further, please let me know:

- Are you looking at **residential, commercial, or mixed-use** schemes?
- Do you need insights tailored to **SME developers** or large-scale institutional borrowing?
